newsitem.title: UK: U.S. funds seen raising international exposure.
newsitem.headline: U.S. funds seen raising international exposure.

text.p: A less impressive U.S. equity market performance in 1997 could spur an increased flow of U.S. funds offshore, SBC Warburg Director John Marsland said.

"We don't really want to see it crash but a less star performance from the U.S. market would be absolutely ideal, say 10 percent or so," he told the Reuters Markets Forum conference. He said U.S. investors accustomed to strong annual stock market gains would be seeking higher yielding investments outside the country if the U.S. market slowed.
"The U.S. retail preoccupation with their own market is not a passing fancy. It is a very equity-oriented culture but I think it has gone a little bit too far."
He said U.S. investors were being advised that they place a reasonably large proportion of their money overseas.
"It is important that they are exposed to these areas. The diversification benefit can't be under-emphasised."
Marsland said he expected global liquidity, currently at its highest level since 1987, to remain high in 1997.
At present price/earnings levels, he said a re-rating was possible in the non-Asian emerging markets, which has already occurred to some extent this year.
"In valuation terms we have got a reasonably optimistic outlook," he said.
"Within global markets as a whole I think attention will be switching to the emerging markets throughout the course of this year."
